chunks: Aban, from Abu al-Abbas, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), he said:
I asked him about the prey of the falcon and the hawk. So he said: 'Do not eat what the falcon and the hawk have killed, and do not eat what the predatory birds have killed.'

key_terms.البازي: Al-Bazi — the falcon (Falco species); used in classical Arabic for trained hunting falcons
key_terms.الصقر: Al-Saqr — the hawk or saker falcon; another bird of prey used in falconry
key_terms.سباع الطير: Siba' al-Tayr — predatory birds; a broader category encompassing all birds that hunt and kill prey with their talons or beaks
key_terms.صيد: Prey/game — hunting or the animal caught; in fiqh, relates to the permissibility of consuming hunted animals

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to eat game killed by falcons or birds of prey according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith records a legal ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) on the permissibility of consuming game killed by birds of prey. The questioner asks about the specific case of falcons and hawks, and the Imam extends the prohibition broadly to include all predatory birds (siba' al-tayr). In classical Islamic jurisprudence, this ruling was understood in the context of hunting: animals killed by trained birds of prey were generally considered halal only under certain conditions, and this narration represents a stricter Shia position prohibiting such game entirely.

en.hubeali:
Aban, from Abu Al Abbas, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘
I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about a prey of the falcon and the hawk. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Do not eat what the falcon and the hawk kill, and do not eat what the predators from the birds kill’.
en.sarwar: 6. Aban has narrated from abu al-‘Abbas who has said the following: “I once asked him (the Imam), ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the hunting of falcons and hawks.
He (the Imam) said, ‘Do not use for food what falcons and hawks kill as well as what the predator birds kill.’”
